chose: reasoning off at the provider registry: moonshot entry returns providerOptions {moonshot:{reasoningEffort:'none'}}, resolveProvider carries it, llm-enrich spreads it into generateText
over: leaving reasoning on and raising LLM_TIMEOUT_MS/maxOutputTokens
passing reasoningEffort from the llm-enrich step
a fetch wrapper injecting reasoning_effort into the body
because: measured on api.moonshot.ai/kimi-k2.6: reasoning on = 8.2s and EMPTY content (thinking spends the same maxOutputTokens budget as the answer, which is what made llm-enrich time out at 60s on a 35-line recipe); off = 0.9s and a correct answer. reasoning_effort='none' works, 'minimal' still thinks, enable_thinking:false is ignored. how a provider must be CALLED is the same kind of fact as where it lives, so it belongs in the registry entry next to baseURL, not at the one call site

chose: rules emitted no gluten and no wheat label at all for a recipe whose dough is 1 kg of flour; the LLM caught both at 0.95
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
en:flour carries no gluten/wheat trait in the food lexicon
the allergen classifier only emits from trait matches and flour resolves to a slug with empty traits, which reads the same as no-allergen
discriminatedBy: look up en:flour in the lexicon and check its traits: present-and-empty vs missing-the-gluten-trait separates them
